silhouette.reason: A raised forebody with a hood over a ground coil reads as a cobra; the hood is narrow and the coil loose.
fixes: wider, flatter hood ribs at the raised neck
tighter coil stack under the raised forebody

proportions.reason: Raised height and coil size plausible for a 3–4 m snake; the body is near-constant girth with a thin tail and an abrupt neck.
fixes: taper girth from mid-body to the tail and swell the mid-body

materials.reason: Dark scales with pale chevrons and cream ventral scutes read as scales; the chevron zigzag is closer to a viper pattern than the king cobra crossbands.
fixes: pale crossbands (chevrons pointing to the head) instead of zigzags
glossy scale roughness (low) on the dorsum

detail.reason: Ventral scutes, head shields and tongue read; no eyes catchlight, no keeled scale normal.
fixes: scale normal map on the flanks

wear.reason: Clean; no shed remnants or scars.
fixes: a dull pre-shed patch or a healed scar

lod.reason: FAR LOD2 replaces the pattern with big black/cream blocks: the colour shifts at distance.
fixes: average the pattern to the dorsal grey-brown at LOD2 instead of sampling per band

technical.reason: QA clean; 62k / 3.8k / 584 tris in one part; the LOD0→LOD1 drop is 16× (a visible pop risk).
fixes: raise LOD1 to ~12k or lower LOD0 ring density along the straight neck
